ruling.recommended_action: Refer to Trust & Safety human review with the case file; keep all chat, GPS speed/timeline telemetry and the driver's statement attached; no fault finding by AI + consider interim_suspension per SAFE-4 pending review.
ruling.reasoning: Dispute type is safety. The rider's complaint states the driver "was speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder" and that the rider "was scared and felt unsafe" [F6-adjacent complaint text; driver statement F6]. This is a dangerous-driving and feeling-unsafe allegation, which triggers the mandatory safety screen (SAFE-1) and the accident/dangerous-driving branch (SAFE-2). Under SAFE-3 the system may only gather evidence, summarise accounts and prepare the case file — it may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome — so no ruling on fare, route or fee is made here. On the screening question itself, the record is consistent with a genuinely fast trip: duration 8.2 min against a 13.8 min estimate [F2], though distance was essentially on-route at 8.3 km vs 8.4 km optimal [F1], so there is no route-deviation issue to decide. The chat shows only pickup arrangements, all timestamped [F3, F4, F5]; the driver denies the allegation and says the rider never complained [F6]. Both profiles are clean, with no fraud flags or upheld disputes [F7, F8], but profile facts never decide a case. No route, no-show or fare element is in issue; the only live question is the safety allegation, which is reserved to a human reviewer. Summary for the reviewer: alleged speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking on the Jurong East MRT → NUS trip of 09:43–09:51; rider felt unsafe; driver denies. Rider should be advised of the 995 emergency line, the driver's commercial motor insurance and RydeHELP (SAFE-2 / A14). Escalation also fits TH-2 (safety → human) and TH-4 is not needed since the safety allegation itself removes the case from system decision.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety dispute: dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) with rider reporting fear/unsafety. Safety cases are reserved to human review; the AI may only prepare the case file (SAFE-1, SAFE-2, SAFE-3).
